review_candidates.title: Founding Edge Intelligence Lead | Robotics & Actuation
review_candidates.description: Location: New York City preferred Company: Eccentric Machines Role type: Full-time Seniority: Senior / Principal / Founding Engineer Compensation: Competitive cash compensation, benefits, and founding-engineer level equity package. This is one of the company’s first technical hires and will carry meaningful ownership, technical authority, and long-term upside tied to building a foundational part of the Sentor platform. About Eccentric Machines Eccentric Machines is building Sentor , a patent-pending AI-native motion platform for robotics and complex electromechanical systems. Sentor is designed to move intelligence closer to the physical motion layer. Instead of treating actuation as a passive output from a central controller, we are building hardware and software that can sense local conditions, adapt to changing loads, and respond in real time. We recently closed our seed round and are building the founding technical team. The Role We are looking for a Founding Edge Intelligence Lead to build the onboard machine learning and decision-making layer for Sentor. This role sits at the intersection of machine learning, robotics, controls, embedded systems, and physical hardware. Your job is to turn signals such as load changes, vibration patterns, motion signatures, thermal behavior, and other physical signals into useful intelligence: state estimation, anomaly detection, adaptive response, and eventually learned motion behavior. This is not a cloud ML role. It is not a dashboard role. It is not a generic AI role. It is the software layer that lets a physical machine learn from its own body. What You’ll Own 1. Onboard Sensing and State Estimation You will develop models and algorithms that interpret Sentor’s local sensor data in real time. This may include: torque resistance estimation; load and contact inference; vibration and resonance mode prediction and detection; friction / hysteresis pattern recognition; thermal and mechanical drift prediction and detection; fatigue / degradation signatures; sensor fusion across current, position, velocity, torque, temperature, strain, vibration, and related signals. The goal is to help Sentor understand what is happening locally before waiting for a centralized robot controller. 2. Edge ML and Local Decision-Making You will build the onboard intelligence layer that enables Sentor to respond intelligently to changing physical conditions. This may include: lightweight ML models for low-power embedded inference; adaptive torque / speed / stiffness response; local reflex-like behaviors; learned response profiles; anomaly detection and protective behaviors; real-time classification of operating regimes; prediction of near-term load or resistance changes; safe local adaptation within guardrails. The system must be fast, robust, and suitable for real-time actuation. Model elegance matters less than useful, reliable behavior on hardware. 3. Controls-Aware Learning This role must bridge ML and controls. You will work on algorithms that can coexist with, augment, or inform control systems rather than fight them. Relevant areas may include: model predictive control; adaptive control; reinforcement learning for constrained physical systems; imitation learning; system identification; state-space models; Kalman filtering / particle filtering; residual learning around physics-based models; learned compensators for friction, hysteresis, backlash, vibration, or load variation. The right person understands that onboard intelligence in an actuator needs to be safe, bounded, and physically grounded. 4. Simulation and Digital Twin Interface You will work closely with our simulation / digital twin function. Over time, the edge intelligence layer should interface with simulation tools so we can: generate synthetic operating scenarios; test edge models before hardware deployment; simulate load changes, impacts, failures, and edge cases; train or validate models in virtual environments; compare simulated sensor traces with real bench data; accelerate sim-to-real iteration; develop motion profiles before physical customer deployments. The long-term vision is for Sentor’s onboard intelligence and Sentor’s simulation environment to reinforce each other. 5. Embedded Deployment You will help turn ML models into deployable real-time software. This will include: embedded C model development and deployment model compression and optimization; embedded inference; latency and memory optimization; real-time data pipelines; firmware / embedded software integration; safety fallbacks; deterministic behavior under constrained compute; deployment to microcontrollers, embedded Linux, DSPs, or edge accelerators. The job is not done when the model works in Python. The job is done when it improves behavior on the machine. Ideal Background Strong candidates have experience with: embedded C code; robotics; autonomous systems; humanoids / legged robots; drones; surgical robotics; industrial automation; motor control; embedded ML/edge AI; controls; physical AI; sensor fusion; reinforcement learning for real systems; predictive maintenance / anomaly detection for machines; simulation-to-real robotics. Relevant experience may include: time-series ML; real-time sensor fusion; embedded inference; controls-aware ML; actuator or motor control; adaptive systems; state estimation; robot dynamics; online learning or calibration; physics-informed ML; digital twins; sim-to-real workflows. Tools and Technical Stack Preferred experience: Embedded C; Python, C++; PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, scikit-learn; ONNX, TensorRT, TFLite Micro, TVM or related deployment tools; MATLAB / Simulink; ROS / ROS 2; MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Gazebo, Drake, or related robotics simulation tools; real-time data acquisition; embedded Linux, RTOS, microcontrollers, DSPs, or edge accelerators; control systems, MPC, state-space modeling, filtering, and system identification. We care less about exact tool overlap and more about whether you can build useful intelligence for real physical systems. What Success Looks Like In the first 3–6 months, success looks like: building the first sensor data pipeline for Sentor; defining the onboard intelligence architecture; identifying which sensor signals are most predictive of physical state; creating initial models for load / resistance / operating-regime inference; deploying early edge models or algorithms on prototype hardware; building safety-bounded local response behaviors; integrating with bench-test data and simulation outputs; helping define how Sentor learns from repeated physical interaction. Longer term, this role becomes foundational to Sentor’s differentiation: local intelligence at the actuator level, coordinated across the robot through Sentor Motion Studio. You Are a Fit If You are excited by ML that touches real hardware. You think physical intelligence should live closer to the body, not only in the cloud or central controller. You can move between Python experiments, embedded C code, control theory, embedded constraints, and physical test data. You understand that real-time systems require safety, reliability, and bounded behavior. You are comfortable building with incomplete data and improving through iteration. You want to help create the onboard intelligence layer for a new category of actuation.

review_candidates.description: Op deze pagina: Dit ga je doen Dit krijg je Dit bieden we nog meer Dit vragen wij Hier kom je te werken Bijzonderheden Stel gerust je vraag Dit ga je doen Binnen de Rechtspraak groeit de behoefte aan AI-oplossingen die het werk ondersteunen. Er is al een eerste toepassing in productie: Rechtspraak GPT. Ook nieuwe toepassingen komen eraan, zoals speech-to-text en het pseudonimiseren van uitspraken. Aan jou de taak om het hybride AI-platform daarachter verder vorm te geven. Hoe richten we dat slim in? Wat is ervoor nodig? En hoe zorgen we dat nieuwe oplossingen landen op een stevige basis? Kortom: werk waarin innovatie en maatschappelijke relevantie samenkomen. Jij verbindt architectuur, techniek en praktijk. Samen met ons datalab en de DevOps-teams die aan ons AI-platform bouwen ontwerp je solutions en vertaal je functionele requirements naar een architectuur die werkt. Je denkt in technische bouwblokken en kijkt naar vraagstukken rond training, deployment, monitoring en integratie in een hybride landschap van OpenShift en Azure. Zo geef je richting aan de grote lijnen én aan de technische keuzes die nodig zijn om meters te maken. Ondertussen ben je ook zichtbaar in de organisatie. Je gaat in gesprek met eindgebruikers, haalt requirements op en vertelt waar het platform staat en waar het naartoe gaat. Dat vraagt om meer dan technische kennis alleen. Je begrijpt dat de AI-geletterdheid binnen de organisatie verschilt en weet daarin goed te schakelen. Juist doordat je de vragen uit de praktijk kent, kun je betere keuzes maken in het ontwerp van het platform en de oplossingen die daarop landen. Wil jij aan de wieg staan van AI binnen de Rechtspraak? Denk je niet alleen graag ideeën uit, maar help je ze ook realiseren? En ben je op je best in een omgeving waar nog niet alles vastligt? Dan is dit jouw rol! review_candidates.description: Company Description At De Beers Group our purpose is to Make Life Brilliant. We believe that a sustainable business is purposeful, competitive, resilient and agile – it’s a business that thrives through both economic and social cycles. By understanding the context and listening to stakeholders we stay ahead of evolving trends and provide the solutions to societal expectations. By solving the physical challenges of mining through relentless innovation, and constantly searching for more responsible ways to do business, we are changing the way our employees and stakeholders experience our business – creating enduring value for all stakeholders. Sustainability is at the heart of our decision-making – it is how we do business. Job Description Information Technology (IT) develops and optimises the engine that powers De Beers’ digital and technology ecosystems, enabling our people to work safely, effectively and sustainably. This is a senior functional leadership role accountable for the effective management, support, governance and continuous improvement of SAP Finance solutions across the organisation. The role provides deep SAP Finance and business-process expertise and works with Finance stakeholders, business process owners, IT teams and service providers to ensure that solutions are stable, compliant, standardised and aligned with business objectives. To own and continuously improve SAP Finance solutions by translating business requirements into effective functional designs, maintaining solution integrity, overseeing service and vendor performance, and enabling Finance transformation through standardised and sustainable technology capabilities. Key Responsibilities SAP Finance functional ownership Act as the functional owner and primary IT point of contact for SAP Finance solutions within the assigned scope. Maintain the functional integrity, standardisation and effective use of the SAP Finance landscape. Translate Finance requirements into sustainable SAP solutions aligned with enterprise architecture, design principles and control requirements. Provide functional guidance on process design, configuration, integration, controls and improvement opportunities. Solution delivery and continuous improvement Lead requirements analysis, solution design, functional specification, configuration, testing, implementation and post-deployment support. Assess enhancement demand based on business value, risk, architectural alignment, supportability and total cost of ownership. Promote standard SAP capabilities and fit-to-standard design, limiting customisation to justified business requirements. Identify opportunities for process simplification, automation, reporting improvement and improved user experience. Ensure solution documentation, test evidence, configuration records and operating procedures remain complete and current. Service and operational management Oversee the performance, availability and support of SAP Finance services against agreed service levels and operating procedures. Lead the resolution of priority incidents and recurring problems, including root-cause analysis, remediation planning and prevention of recurrence. Monitor service trends and drive measurable service improvement actions. Coordinate clear and timely stakeholder communication during service disruptions and material delivery risks. Provide functional coaching and knowledge transfer to business users, support teams and delivery partners. Vendor and commercial management Manage functional delivery by SAP support and implementation partners. Monitor supplier performance against contractual commitments, service levels, quality measures and delivery outcomes. Review estimates, statements of work and solution proposals for completeness, value, feasibility and alignment with requirements. Strengthen internal knowledge and documentation to reduce operational dependency on external providers. Governance, risk and compliance Ensure SAP Finance solutions comply with applicable IT controls, security standards, financial control requirements and organisational policies. Support audit activities, user access reviews, control testing, evidence provision and remediation within the SAP Finance domain. Ensure changes follow approved architecture, change, testing, release and deployment governance. Identify technology, service and process risks, assess potential business impact and coordinate corrective actions. Participate in relevant design, change, service and governance forums. Stakeholder and project leadership Partner with Finance stakeholders, process owners and IT teams to maintain a transparent and prioritised demand pipeline. Communicate service performance, decisions, dependencies, risks and delivery progress to relevant stakeholders. Lead or participate in SAP Finance projects, upgrades, migrations and transformation initiatives. Coordinate cross-functional delivery across SAP and integrated applications to achieve end-to-end business outcomes. Work safely, act as a safety leader and consider risks to people and the environment before undertaking activities. Qualifications Relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional qualification in Information Technology, Finance, Accounting, Business Systems or a related discipline. Substantial hands-on functional experience supporting or implementing SAP Finance solutions in a complex enterprise environment. Demonstrated configuration and process knowledge across the SAP Finance capabilities within the role’s defined scope. Experience across the solution lifecycle, including requirements, design, configuration, functional specification, testing, deployment and production support. Experience managing SAP application support or implementation partners and reviewing delivery estimates and proposals. Experience in incident, problem, change and release management within an enterprise service environment. Demonstrated stakeholder management experience with senior Finance and IT stakeholders. Experience working across multiple business units, legal entities or countries in a multinational and multicultural environment. SAP Finance certification is preferred. Current SAP S/4HANA Finance certification is advantageous. Required Functional And Technical Capability Strong knowledge of SAP Finance and Controlling processes and configuration relevant to the assigned scope, which may include General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Asset Accounting, cost and profit centre accounting, internal orders and financial close. Understanding of end-to-end Finance processes, financial controls and the implications of system design for data quality, reporting and auditability. Knowledge of SAP integration with related domains, including Sales and Distribution, Materials Management, Project Systems, Plant Maintenance and external applications. Ability to produce high-quality business requirements, functional designs, specifications, process maps, test scenarios and support documentation. Knowledge of SAP application lifecycle management, transport and release controls, service management and production support practices. Understanding of enterprise architecture, cyber security, access controls, data governance and change governance relevant to SAP Finance. Ability to analyse complex incidents and requirements, identify root causes and recommend sustainable solutions. Practical experience with SAP S/4HANA Finance and relevant SAP Fiori applications. Participation in an SAP S/4HANA implementation, migration, conversion or major Finance transformation. Advantageous capability Experience with SAP Joint Venture Accounting in a mining, resources or multinational operating environment. Exposure to SAP Treasury, profitability analysis, product costing, Group Reporting or other specialist Finance capabilities relevant to the application landscape. Experience with reporting, analytics, workflow or intelligent automation capabilities that support Finance processes. Additional Information Our Values Put Safety First We consider all risks to people and the environment before proceeding with any activity. We address risks before beginning any activity, even if this means stopping a task. Zero Harm is always our goal. Be Passionate We are exhilarated by the product we sell, the challenges we face and the opportunities we create. Pull Together Being united in purpose and action, we will turn the diversity of our people, skills and experience into an unparalleled source of strength. Build Trust We will always listen first, then act with openness, honesty and integrity so that our relationships flourish Show We Care The people whose lives we touch, their communities, nations and the environment we share, all matter deeply to us. We will always think through the consequences of what we do so that our contribution to the world is real, lasting and makes us proud. Shape the Future We will find new ways. We will set demanding targets and take both tough decisions and considered risks to achieve them. We will insist on excellent execution and reward those who deliver. Closing Date: 05 October 2026

REES is housed within the School of Arts & Sciences, which is comprised of the College of Arts and Sciences, the Graduate Division, and the College of Liberal and Professional Studies. Through departmental curricula as well as those of the Penn Language Center, students have access to education in Russian, Czech, Hungarian, Polish, Ukrainian, Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian, and other languages of the region. We contribute to the education of graduate students in several neighboring disciplines, including Anthropology, Comparative Literature, History, Political Science, and others.
